note: The two sets are nearly identical in content: both capture the same section sizes (C3X6, W8X10, W10X12, L3X3X1/4, L4X4X5/16, PL5X3/8, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2, HSS 4X4X1/4) and the same dimensions (1'-4", 2'-4 1/2", 10", 8", 6", 4", 1/4" TYP). The only difference is that A states the W8X10 section a third time as 'structural member | section profile' while B states it as 'member | section' — both are duplicates of the W-beam W8X10 claim. Both sets share the same weaknesses: duplicated facts under different entity names, vague 'component' entities for bare dimensions, the 2'-4 1/2" length carrying a TYP condition that likely belongs to the 1/4" weld, and the keynote number 05 12 23.A7 misbound as a specification of the HSS member.
remarks: Both extractions treat the reference keynote number 05 12 23.A7 as a 'specification' of HSS 4 X 4 X 1/4; on the page it is a keynote reference, not a material/spec designation. The TYP qualifier in the quote 'TYP 1/4" 2'-4 1/2"' appears to apply to the 1/4" dimension (likely a weld or gap), not to the 2'-4 1/2" length. Many bare dimensions (6", 8", 4", 10") are extracted with generic 'component' entities because the text layer provides no reliable binding to a specific member; the image would be needed to bind them correctly. Both sets also omit several facts present on the page (e.g. 5 7/8", 1 13/16", 11 1/2", 1'-3", W10X15, HSS4X4X1/4 in the second detail, 5 1/8", 1 3/8", 5/8", 1 1/2' scale dimensions), though these are mostly minor detail dimensions.
